review_notes: I read the whole target file. The only @[simp] lemmas are the two block-vector round-trip lemmas, and they look fine. I then grepped the sibling files (NewtonSystem, LocalNeighborhoodEstimates, FixedYTMTheory, GeneratedConvergence) to see how addStep, ones, bbar, cbar and toHSDirection are actually used. The findings are about missing canonical simp lemmas. I did not recommend simp lemmas for matVec, tMatVec, dot, mu or gap. Those would unfold sums or divisions and would compete with the existing matVec_smul_apply / dot_smul_right style lemmas. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour or loops. I did not check whether the sibling files already define lemmas such as addStep_x. The grep for 'addStep' shows only dsimp [addStep] / unfold uses.

findings.problem: `addStep` returns a structure, but the file gives no simp lemmas for its projections. Downstream proofs about `(addStep w d α).x i`, `.tau`, `.s i` and `.kappa` have to unfold the definition by hand. The sibling files do this about ten times with `dsimp [addStep]` and several times with `unfold gap addStep hdot`. Because `mu` and `gap` are also unfolded by hand, these proofs expand `addStep` and the surrounding definitions together instead of rewriting through a stable normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Add field-projection simp lemmas proved by `rfl`: `@[simp] addStep_x (w d α i) : (addStep w d α).x i = w.x i + α * d.dx i`, and likewise `addStep_tau`, `addStep_s` and `addStep_kappa`. The right-hand sides are strictly smaller expressions, so there is no cycle. Calls like `dsimp [addStep]` can then become plain `simp`/`simp only [addStep_x, …]`.
findings.benefit: Users reason about `addStep` through its four component identities rather than through its definition body. Proof scripts such as `corrector_component_product_full_step` become shorter and more robust, and `addStep` no longer has to be unfolded by name at each use site.

findings.excerpt:
def cbar {m n : Nat} (P : LPData m n) : Vec n :=
  fun j => P.c j - 1
findings.problem: `ones`, `bbar` and `cbar` are defined as bare lambdas, and no applied-form simp lemmas exist for them. `simp` therefore cannot rewrite `(ones : Vec n) i` to `1`, `cbar P j` to `P.c j - 1`, or `bbar P i` to `P.b i - matVec P.A ones i`. The consequence is visible in `NewtonSystem.lean`. The proof of the Schur-complement step uses `unfold dot ones`, then writes out the intermediate `1 * tMatVec …` terms in a calc. A later step needs `unfold zbar cbar dot ones` before `simp [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]` can proceed. Without a canonical form for `ones i`, `1 * _` residues must be cleaned up by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem ones_apply {n} (i : Fin n) : (ones : Vec n) i = 1 := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem cbar_apply (P) (j) : cbar P j = P.c j - 1 := rfl`. Optionally add `bbar_apply (P) (i) : bbar P i = P.b i - matVec P.A ones i := rfl`, and keep `bbar_apply` non-simp if expanding `bbar` is not wanted. Do not make `matVec_apply` or `dot` simp lemmas. Those would unfold sums and compete with the existing `matVec_smul_apply` and `dot_smul_right` rules.
findings.benefit: The vector `ones` and the shifted cost `cbar` get one canonical simp normal form, so `simp` reduces `dot ones (cbar P)` style goals through `one_mul` and `Finset.sum_sub_distrib` without `unfold` of several definitions. This removes the hand-unfolding and the manual `1 * …` calc steps in the nondegeneracy proof of the HLP block system.

findings.excerpt: def HLPFullDirection.toHSDirection {m n : Nat} (D : HLPFullDirection m n) : HSDirection n :=
findings.problem: This is another structure-valued projection map, and it has no `@[simp]` field lemmas. Uses must either unfold it by name (`unfold HLPFullDirection.toHSDirection hdot`) or pass it to `simpa [HLPFullDirection.toHSDirection, hdot]`. Both forms rely on the definition body rather than a simp interface, even though the file already gives `@[simp]` round-trip lemmas for the sibling conversion `toBlockVector`/`ofBlockVector`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem HLPFullDirection.toHSDirection_dx (D) : D.toHSDirection.dx = D.dx := rfl`, and likewise for `dtau`, `ds` and `dkappa`. Alternatively, mark the definition `@[simps]`. The right-hand sides are plain projections, so there is no cycle risk.
findings.benefit: The reduced-direction conversion is as simp-friendly as the block-vector conversion in the same file. Callers can use `simp [hdot]` or `simp only [toHSDirection_dx, …]` instead of unfolding the definition, and goals about `hdot D.toHSDirection.dx …` reduce to expressions in the full-direction fields.
